messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Severity P1 — high-rate GPU OOMs on decode-streaming. Affected: /v1/stream (prod, us-west). Error symptom: CUDA OOM followed by container restart; ~18% of streaming requests returned 5xx in last 5m. Paging on-call: @jordan-oncall and SRE.
jordan-oncall: On it. Observing sustained spike in decode error traces. Reassigning to @ashley-sre for containment + root cause triage. Who owns model routing? @dmitri-ml?
ashley-sre: I can take containment. Quick telemetry: nodes 10.3.12.[4-7] showing repeated oom with kernel msg "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY" and process crashloop. Streaming RT latency also spiked. Suspect runaway generation / header max_tokens bypassing request caps. Will try fast mitigations: token cap at edge, enable CPU fallback, and isolate offending keys.
dmitri-ml: I see a concurrent increase in token counts per request (token hist tail moved from 120 to >10k for a subset). Looks like some clients sending large max_tokens or content leading to unbounded generation. Also KV-cache growth on decode nodes. Running a query to map top API keys by token usage.
ashley-sre: Steps I'm going to run now:
1) push emergency token cap on ingress to 2k tokens for streaming routes
2) enable fallback route for streaming decode to cpu-decode pool for short term
3) block offending API keys after identification
4) scale up decode-fallback replica count + increase eviction thresholds to reduce restarts
jordan-oncall: +1. Please post commands you run so we have traceability.
ashley-sre: Running commands:
```
# edge: enforce per-request token cap
curl -X POST "https://ingress.internal/api/v1/configs" -d '{"route":"/v1/stream","max_tokens_override":2000}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"

# route change: add cpu-decode fallback
curl -X POST "https://router.internal/api/v1/routes/fallback" -d '{"route":"/v1/stream","fallback":"cpu-decode","weight":100}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"

# identify top API keys by token consumption in last 10m
psql -At -c "select api_key, sum(tokens) from requests where route='/v1/stream' and ts > now() - interval '10 minutes' group by api_key order by sum desc limit 20;"
```
ops-bot: Node status update: cordon+drain in progress for node 10.3.12.6; container restarts paused on 10.3.12.5; fallback pool scaled to 6 replicas.
dmitri-ml: Query results: three keys stand out (key_ak_42, key_ak_77, key_ak_99) — combined responsible for ~72% of high-token requests. Also seeing unusual content patterns: many requests include a prompt suffix like "continue indefinitely" and missing max_tokens header from some SDK versions.
ashley-sre: I'm going to add temporary denylist for those API keys at the edge and throttle them to zero for streaming while we contact owners. Applying now.
maria-cs: Who are the affected customers? Need a short blurb for customer ops and CS to send to impacted accounts. Also need ETA for mitigation.
jordan-oncall: @ashley-sre can you prepare impact numbers (requests dropped, % of traffic, tenant count)? We should also draft an admin-facing status blurb.
ashley-sre: Impact snapshot (last 15m): total streaming reqs = 54k, dropped/failed = 9.7k (~18%), affected tenants = 8 (5 with >=1% of their traffic impacted). Mitigation ETA: token cap and fallback applied (currently rolling), expected full stabilization in 8-12 minutes pending node restarts finishing. Draft message below.
ashley-sre: Draft for CS/admin channel:
"We're investigating intermittent streaming failures caused by large/unbounded generations that triggered GPU OOMs on decode nodes. We've applied an emergency per-request token cap and routed streaming traffic to a CPU fallback pool for stability. A small number of API keys have been temporarily throttled while we contact the owners. We expect error rates to return to normal within ~10 minutes. If your team sees continued failures, please escalate to cs@redwood.com."
maria-cs: Good. Can we include the list of impacted tenants (anonymized if needed) and whether any SLA credit applies?
ashley-sre: I'll share anonymized tenant IDs to CS. SLA credit review: will coordinate with finance/team after full RCA. For now focus on containment.
jordan-oncall: Ops note — we've avoided mass pod restarts by adding eviction headroom; a few nodes still OOM'd and were recycled. Error rate trending down: current 5xx ~4.8% (was ~18%). Keep monitoring.
ops-bot: Telemetry: 5xx rate over last 5m: 4.8%. GPU memory pressure decreased on drained nodes. Fallback pool CPU utilization increased to 70%.
dmitri-ml: Root cause candidate: a subset of SDK versions (v0.9.1) do not send max_tokens in some streaming flows; in combination with a prompt pattern we flagged, that allowed unbounded generation. We'll open a fix in the SDK to default max_tokens and add server-side hard caps.
ashley-sre: Post-mitigation tasks I will own:
- remove denylist after owners contacted and throttle lifted
- add permanent server-side hard cap for streaming routes
- add metric alert on token-percentile spikes (95th/99th)
- RCA doc with timeline + customers impacted
maria-cs: I'll prepare customer outreach templates and start contacting the 3 primary affected accounts. Thanks for the ETA.
jordan-oncall: Handoff to next oncall @ashley-sre for overnight monitoring. Remaining tasks for follow-up: collect kernel OOM dumps, correlate request ids to crash dumps, and push SDK patch. If error rate rises >6% escalate immediately. Leaving incident channel open for updates.
incident-bot: UPDATE: Mitigations applied (token cap + cpu-fallback + denylist). Error rate reduced to 4.8%. Pager cleared for active action; ongoing follow-ups assigned. Incident record: INC-2026-03-15-056 (owner: ashley-sre).
ashley-sre: Quick note for postmortem: timeline, commands executed, API keys throttled, impacted tenant counts, and proposed permanent controls (server hard cap, SDK patch, per-key rate-limits). Will start RCA draft and tag @dmitri-ml and @maria-cs.
maria-cs: Thanks all — drafting customer notes and scheduling a sync with affected customers in 1h.
